A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COGT research. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A-F are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original COGT benchmark evaluations, ablations, downstream classification results, computational measurements and qualitative examples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original COGT evaluations, ablations, classification results, computational measurements and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The dependency-parser-derived CGM, dependency-guided decoder, syntactic mask tokens, training objective and inference procedure remain unchanged, including the tokenization handling in Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both versions retain COCO, CC3M and Visual Genome training, the five main compositional benchmarks, appendix Winoground/MMVP evaluations, and CIFAR/ImageNet classification tasks. The added comparator uses existing ARO coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds CLIP-SPEC (Peng et al., 2024) to Table 3's ARO comparison under methods trained on datasets larger than COCO. Other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations and evaluation procedures are retained. Appendix D.3 still specifies 10 epochs, batch size 128 and the same checkpoint-selection procedure; the added CLIP-SPEC row introduces no separately specified protocol.

E4.justification: The prediction-strategy, parser, mask-token and visual-layer ablations in Tables 1, 2 and 7 are unchanged. The computational analysis and qualitative successes/failures in Appendix C.4 and Figures 4-12 are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals or statistical significance tests. Appendix C.2 retains the same caution about MMVP's small sample size.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds CLIP-SPEC scores of 73.70 for ARO Relation, 66.40 for Attribute and 70.05 average. Matched pre-existing numerical and qualitative results remain unchanged; Table 10's 56.20 versus 56.2 is equivalent formatting.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(5), the CGM definition, independence assumptions and Appendix A's sparsity argument are unchanged. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical revision is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims about CGM-guided generation, avoiding spurious dependencies and outperforming previous compositional approaches, including methods trained on larger datasets.

C2.justification: The causal interpretation and qualifications, parser-quality discussion, noisy-caption interpretation, MMVP small-sample caveat and Winoground weakness are retained in Section 3 and Appendices A and C.

D1.justification: The first-page access link changes from the GitHub repository to the project website. Both versions already state that code and model weights are available; implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and timing information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bolelli et al. (2018) alongside the discussion of parallel caption prediction and Peng et al. (2024) for compositional benchmarking and CLIP-SPEC. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited edits update affiliation, publication status and acknowledgments, place the availability statement in the abstract, and correct 'Grafical' to 'Graphical' in Appendix A. The section organization and scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds conference headers and page numbers, resizes several figures and tables, and adjusts their placement, including moving Figure 4 from page 22 to page 23. Table 3 gains the CLIP-SPEC row; the existing diagrams and qualitative examples are preserved.

improvement.justification: Adding CLIP-SPEC's ARO results in Table 3 modestly improves comparison completeness, with existing evidence and appendix detail preserved. This small gain is partly offset by smaller main-text diagrams and tables. The method, validation scope and conclusions otherwise remain unchanged.
